diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 3.3 V, datasheet reading 4.75 V
diffs.evidence: The 4.75 V figure is Seeed's nominal 5 V Seeeduino spec, but the board is a bare 10 kOhm pot divider and Seeed's own wiki example runs it from 3.3 V ('the other side pin to VCC (3.3V)') and notes 'If the Vcc switch on the seeeduino board switches to 3V3, the ADC_REF should be 3.3', so 3.3 V is a supported (and, for 3.3 V ADCs, the safe) supply; the 4.75-5.25 V table value is noted in the model's buildNotes.

diffs.diff: angle (deg): datasheet reading gives 60 per count, the part's model has 90.91
diffs.evidence: Seeed's formula is 'float degrees = ( voltage * FULL_ANGLE ) / GROVE_VCC' with 'full value of the rotary angle is 300 degrees', i.e. 300/VCC degrees per volt: 300/5 = 60 deg/V at the wiki's 5 V and 300/3.3 = 90.91 deg/V at the model's 3.3 V supply, so the two scales are the same formula at different VCC.
